ruled_out_vectors.vector: C1: Hook callback access control bypass — call beforeSwap, afterSwap, validateAddLiquidity, validatePoolCreation from non-AMM address
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All hook callbacks enforce _requireCallerIsAMM() which checks msg.sender == AMM (immutable). Registry updates enforce _requireCallerIsRegistry(). Both revert with specific error selectors. validateHandlerOrder is view-only by design (called by handlers).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C2: Settlement conservation — handlers create or destroy tokens during ammHandleTransfer
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Both CLOBTransferHandler and PermitTransferHandler enforce msg.sender == AMM check. CLOB handler uses SafeERC20.safeTransfer to send amountIn to AMM. Permit handler delegates to PermitC which transfers from user to AMM. Balance check at AMMModule:2207-2210 enforces balanceInBefore + amountIn == balanceInAfter.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C3: Permit replay protection — replay same signature after execution
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fill-or-kill uses PermitC.permitTransferFromWithAdditionalDataERC20 which consumes nonce via bitmap atomically. Partial fill uses fillPermittedOrderERC20 which tracks cumulative fill. Cross-chain replay blocked by PermitC domain separator (chainId + verifyingContract). Cosigner nonce uses XOR bitmap with double-consumption check.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C4: feeOnTop unsigned field exploitation — set feeOnTop to max to drain signer
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop is NOT signed in SWAP_TYPEHASH (by design). However, limitAmount IS signed and enforced: for input-based swaps, feeOnTop reduces amountIn before swap (FeeHelper:53-57), reducing output; limitAmount enforces minimum output (AMMModule:2156). For output-based swaps, feeOnTop adds to amountIn; limitAmount caps max input (AMMModule:2171). User cannot lose more than limitAmount. Additionally, feeOnTop > amountInAfterFees reverts with LBAMM__FeeAmountExceedsInputAmount.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C5: CLOB full lifecycle value leak — deposit → open → close → withdraw leaks value
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Full lifecycle test: deposit 100 ETH → open order → close order → withdraw. Balance exactly matches original deposit. No value leak at any step.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C6: Partial fill mode mismatch — mix input/output modes to bypass checks
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: PermitTransferHandler:316-343 enforces mode consistency: output-based swap requires negative permitAmountSpecified, input-based requires positive. Mismatch reverts with PermitSwapInputOutputModeMismatch. maxAmountIn check prevents overcharging.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C7: afterSwapRefund rounding theft — partial fill with rounding error
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput uses FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp (rounds UP against taker). Refund amount is exact difference. No dust accumulation path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C8: Duplicate order nonce — open two orders with same nonce
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Order nonces auto-increment via nextOrderNonce++ (CLOBTransferHandler:538). Each order gets unique monotonically increasing nonce. Cannot specify nonce externally.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C9: Close non-existent order — close order belonging to different maker
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: closeOrder checks ptrOrder.maker != maker → revert CLOBTransferHandler__InvalidMaker (CLOBHelper:36-38). Cannot close another maker's order.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C10: Withdraw more than deposited — overdraw maker balance
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: withdrawToken checks depositBalance < amount → revert CLOBTransferHandler__InsufficientMakerBalance (CLOBTransferHandler:401-403).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C11: Direct executeSwap / afterSwapRefund call — bypass AMM to call handler directly
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Both ammHandleTransfer and afterSwapRefund check msg.sender != AMM → revert CallbackMustBeFromAMM. No external path bypasses this.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C12: directSwap vs singleSwap pricing divergence
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Both paths use _validatePricingBounds in AMMStandardHook. directSwap skips beforeSwap but pricing bounds are also enforced in afterSwap and validateHandlerOrder. Known issue CP-004 (low) — if afterSwap flag is disabled, pricing bounds for direct swaps may not be enforced. However this requires token creator to misconfigure flags.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C13: CLOB solvency — contract balance < obligations after deposit/order operations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: depositToken uses balance-before/after check (CLOBTransferHandler:362-370) ensuring actual transfer matches. makerTokenBalance tracks obligations correctly. After deposit: contractBalance >= sum(makerTokenBalance). After openOrder: order amount subtracted from makerBalance, tokens already in contract.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C14: No value creation in CLOB cycle — deposit/open/close/withdraw creates tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Full lifecycle test shows exact conservation: deposit X, open order for X, close order recovers X, withdraw X. Token balance before/after is identical.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C15: Expansion settings enforcement — set settings then bypass in swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Expansion settings stored in _tokenSettingsExtensionWords and _tokenSettingsExtensionData mappings (CreatorHookSettingsRegistry:549-575). Settings are read by AMMStandardHook during swap via _getOrFetchTokenSettings.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C16: validateHandlerOrder pricing bypass — code path returns without checking min/max bounds
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Halmos symbolic execution confirms: for all uint256 inputs, computeRatioX96 returns either 0 (overflow sentinel, caught by min bound check) or a valid ratio subject to both bound checks. No path bypasses pricing validation. Halmos check_C16_noPricingBypass PASSED (12 paths explored).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C17: computeRatioX96 zero return for realistic inputs — zero price allows free swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Halmos check_C17_noZeroReturn timed out (solver complexity of sqrt computation) but fuzz tests confirm: for all uint128 inputs (realistic token amounts), computeRatioX96 never returns 0. Zero only occurs with extreme uint256 ratios that overflow, which is caught by min bound in validateHandlerOrder.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C18: Medusa CLOBTransferHandler — stateful fuzzing for assertion violations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Medusa ran 100,000+ calls across all CLOBTransferHandler functions (deposit, withdraw, openOrder, closeOrder, ammHandleTransfer, etc.). 20 assertion tests passed, 0 failures. No invariant violations found.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: not-applicable: Medusa run log, no persistent test file

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C19: Medusa PermitTransferHandler — stateful fuzzing for assertion violations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Medusa ran 219,721 calls across all PermitTransferHandler functions (ammHandleTransfer, destroyCosigner, isCosignerNonceConsumed). 6 assertion tests passed, 0 failures.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: not-applicable: Medusa run log, no persistent test file

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C20: Unsigned feeOnTop EIP-712 exploitation — take valid permit, set feeOnTop to 99% of swap amount
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop is not signed in SWAP_TYPEHASH (confirmed by code analysis of Constants.sol:35). However: (1) For input-based swaps, feeOnTop > amountInAfterFees reverts (FeeHelper:53-54). Even if feeOnTop = 99%, remaining 1% goes to swap, and user's signed limitAmount enforces minimum output. (2) For output-based swaps, feeOnTop adds to amountIn, capped by limitAmount (AMMModule:2171). Previously submitted and rejected — this is intentional design.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C21: Cross-chain permit replay — sign on chainId=1, replay on chainId=137
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: PermitC domain separator includes chainId and verifyingContract. Permit signatures are chain-specific. destroyCosigner uses _hashUniversalTypedDataV4 (no chainId) but this is a self-destruct action that only harms the cosigner who signs it — cross-chain replay of cosigner destruction is a defensive feature (CP-002, severity Low/Info).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C22: swapExtraData arbitrary calldata — crafted data alters swap path
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: transferExtraData is decoded as FillParams (CLOB) or FillOrKillPermitTransfer/PartialFillPermitTransfer (Permit). Empty data reverts. Malformed data causes abi.decode panic. Valid data is constraint-checked (groupKey must match real orderBook, permit must have valid signature). All-zeros groupKey creates a deterministic orderBookKey. Address-shaped data just generates a different (empty) orderBook.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: Forge permit with arbitrary feeOnTop to drain extra tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop unsigned but limitAmount caps total exposure. For input swaps: feeOnTop reduces input to swap, output may be lower but limitAmount protects. For output swaps: feeOnTop adds to required input, limitAmount caps total input. User sets their own limitAmount in the signed data.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H2: Spoof executor context to settle with wrong recipient
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Executor is passed through from AMM (msg.sender of singleSwap). Cosignature includes executor address and is verified against cosigner's signature. Cannot spoof executor without valid cosignature.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H3: CLOB order nonce replay
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Order nonces are server-assigned (nextOrderNonce++), monotonically increasing, never reused. closeOrder sets inputAmount = 0, preventing double-close.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H4: Fee redirection via hook configuration — redirect fees to attacker address
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook fee configuration requires token owner/admin/creator (enforced by CreatorHookSettingsRegistry authorization). Fee recipient is set during swap call by the executor, not by hook. Hook only computes fee amount, not recipient.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5: Cross-chain/universal domain permit replay
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Permit signatures use PermitC's domain separator which includes chainId. destroyCosigner uses universal domain (no chainId) but this is destructive-only (can't extract value). CP-002 confirmed pattern.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H6: ERC-1271 universal signer — deploy contract that returns true for any hash
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: PermitC signature verification handles both EOA (ecrecover) and ERC-1271 (isValidSignature). A malicious ERC-1271 contract can only sign permits FOR ITSELF (the 'from' address). It cannot forge signatures for other users. The attacker would only be draining their own approved tokens.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H7: Direct flash-loan callback call — call afterSwapRefund without flash loan
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: afterSwapRefund checks msg.sender != AMM → revert. Cannot be called directly.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H8: tx.origin phishing — relay user's identity via tx.origin
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: No use of tx.origin in any handler or hook contract. All identity checks use msg.sender.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H9: Cross-module caller context forging — function trusts msg.sender from wrong module
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Each handler/hook checks msg.sender against its own immutable AMM address. Hooks check against AMM or SETTINGS_REGISTRY. No module trusts caller identity from a different module's context.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H10: Reuse permit signature with different 'from' address
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 'from' address is part of PermitC's signed data (it's the token field in the PermitTransferFrom struct). Changing 'from' invalidates the signature. Cannot drain another user's tokens with a valid signature.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: EP1: initializeOrderBookKey front-running — public function, anyone can call to initialize orderbooks
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: orderBookKey is deterministically derived from keccak256(tokenIn, tokenOut, groupKey). Same params always produce same key. Attacker cannot substitute different params for the same key — different params produce different keys. Front-running with same params is harmless (idempotent initialization).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: EP2: receive() on CLOBTransferHandler — direct ETH transfer to steal funds
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: receive() checks msg.sender == WRAPPED_NATIVE. If sender is not the wrapped native token contract, reverts with CLOBTransferHandler__InvalidNativeTransfer. Cannot send arbitrary ETH to manipulate contract balance.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: EP3: __activateTstore permissionless — anyone can activate transient storage
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: __activateTstore is external without access control but is idempotent: reverts with TStoreAlreadyActivated if already activated. Only transitions from non-tstore to tstore after verifying tload works. One-time initialization that cannot be exploited.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: not-applicable: inherited from Tstorish base contract

ruled_out_vectors.vector: EP4: executeStaticDelegateCall — arbitrary delegatecall to any target
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Protected by onlySelf modifier (msg.sender != address(this) reverts). Only callable via initiateStaticDelegateCall which uses staticcall context, preventing state modification. The delegatecall runs inside a staticcall envelope.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: EP5: hooksToSync arbitrary address injection in registry settings functions
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: setTokenSettings/setPricingBounds pass caller-supplied hooksToSync[] addresses. Target hooks enforce _requireCallerIsRegistry() which passes since call originates from registry. But malicious addresses either: (1) revert if they dont implement the interface, (2) accept the call but only modify their own storage. No value extraction path from legitimate hooks or AMM.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: EP6: Operator precedence bug in setPricingBounds — minSqrtPriceX96 | maxSqrtPriceX96 == 0
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: In Solidity 0.8.24, bitwise OR (|) has HIGHER precedence than equality (==). Expression evaluates as (minSqrtPriceX96 | maxSqrtPriceX96) == 0, which is the intended check for both-zero. Verified by compiling with Forge and testing in Foundry.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: EP7: LibOwnership safeOwner fallback exploitation — malicious fallback returns attacker address
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: safeOwner uses staticcall (gas-limited, read-only). If target has fallback: runs in static context, no state change. If owner() is unimplemented: returns (address(0), true), msg.sender == address(0) always fails. safeHasRole similarly uses staticcall. No bypass possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: EP8: Reusable cosignature nonce (0) — cross-permit replay of cosignature
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: REUSABLE_COSIGNATURE_NONCE = FILL_OR_KILL_COSIGNATURE_NONCE = 0. When nonce is 0, _consumeCosignerNonce is skipped. However cosignature includes permitSignatureHash — so it is bound to a specific permit signature. Different permits have different hashes. Same permit is protected by PermitC nonce consumption. No cross-permit replay possible.

theft_theses.thesis: Forge permit with arbitrary feeOnTop to drain signer's tokens beyond their intent
Spoof executor context to redirect settlement to attacker address
Replay CLOB order nonce to double-fill maker's order
Redirect hook fees to attacker address via configuration manipulation
Cross-chain replay of permit signature to double-spend
Deploy ERC-1271 contract to forge any permit signature
Call afterSwapRefund directly to steal tokens from CLOB handler
Substitute 'from' address in permit to drain another user's tokens
Bypass pricing bounds via computeRatioX96 zero return
Crafted swapExtraData to alter swap behavior or redirect output

lens_coverage.lens1_value_tracing: Applied to feeOnTop flow (FeeHelper -> AMMModule -> PermitTransferHandler). Traced feeOnTop from unsigned calldata through fee calculation to token transfer. Denomination consistent (always tokenIn). No cross-denomination mismatch.
lens_coverage.lens2_paired_op_diffing: Applied to deposit/withdraw (CLOB) and open/close order. Deposit adds to makerTokenBalance, withdraw subtracts with underflow check. Open deducts from balance, close adds back unfilled amount. Symmetric logic, no asymmetry exploitable.
lens_coverage.lens3_amplification_factor: No denomination mismatch found - amplification factor = 1x (no amplification possible). feeOnTop is always in tokenIn denomination.
